title: Jonah: the prophet who ran from mercy
note: Rebuilt on 2026-11-26 from the Bible Explorer film of the same slug. New wording, same facts: each claim is in the old film's captions or its 'differ' note, whose sources are in docs/work/elite/explorer-ledger.md. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, checked against client/public/bible/text/ by film/tools/write-script.py.

lines: Jonah is unlike the other prophets. It's almost all story, with one short sentence of prophecy.
God sends Jonah to Nineveh, a great city of Assyria, Israel's enemy. Jonah boards a ship for Tarshish, at the far end of the known world.

scripture.text: Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.

lines: It has four chapters. Jonah runs, and the sailors fear the LORD. His prayer from the depths. Nineveh turns. Then Jonah's anger, and God's question.
The last chapter is the real climax, and the book ends on a question Jonah never answers.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: all of it obeys
lines: Jonah confesses the LORD as the God who made the sea and the dry land, and the book shows it. God appoints a storm, a fish, a plant, a worm, and an east wind.
Everything in the book obeys God except his prophet.

scripture.text: Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah

chapters.kicker: Watch for: down, and up again
lines: Jonah goes down to the port, down into the ship, down to the roots of the mountains. From the fish he prays a psalm of thanks, and God brings him up.
But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!
Jesus took this as the sign of Jonah, a picture of his own death, burial, and resurrection.

scripture.text: But You raised my life from the pit, O LORD my God!

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the city that turned
lines: The sailors, a king, and a whole city respond to God more readily than his prophet does. Jonah's warning offers no mercy, yet Nineveh turns, and God relents.
His warnings of judgment are meant to lead people to turn.

scripture.text: He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the question at the end
lines: Jonah is furious, and he explains why he ran.
I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger.
God gives him a plant, then takes it away, and ends the book with a question.

scripture.text: I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger

lines: Many readers, Jewish and Christian, take Jonah as history. Many others read it as a teaching story. Some hold both.
Whatever a reader decides, the book's message is the same.
Start with chapter one and read all four. Watch three words: great, down, and appointed.
The worst misreading argues about the fish and misses the question about mercy.

scripture.text: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh

lines: Jonah never answers that question. It's asked of the reader too.
titleCard: The question is asked of you too.
